best_for: Freelancers and consultants on Windows who bill by the hour and want their computer to log what they worked on, so timesheets come from data instead of memory.
description:
ManicTime is a time tracker from Finkit d.o.o., a company that has sold it since 2007. Instead of asking you to start and stop a timer, it runs in the background and writes down which apps, websites and documents you had open, and when.

Later you look at the day as a timeline and assign blocks of it to the right client, project or task. It notices when you step away and lets you say what happened in that gap. It can also record Git branches, file paths, window titles and web addresses, and tell office days from remote days by your IP address. Your data can flow to tools such as Jira, GitHub, Asana and QuickBooks Online.

points.title: Free on Windows, with limits
points.text: ManicTime says its free Windows version can be used in any setting. Auto tagging, timesheets, alerts, advanced search, the tag editor, scheduled backups and password protection need a license.

points.title: Mac means paying
points.text: The Mac and Linux versions come with ManicTime Pro or a cloud plan, not with the free version. The installers here are 30-day trials.

points.title: Cloud plans by the month
points.text: Standard is listed at USD 9 per user per month for 3 devices and cloud backup. Ultimate is USD 11 for 5 devices and cloud screenshots, and Ultimate AI is USD 20 with AI tagging. Yearly billing saves 20%. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: Or buy once and keep your data
points.text: The on-premise Pro license is a one-time payment per user that includes a self-hosted ManicTime Server and a year of upgrades. After that year you keep the last version you got or renew. All data stays on your own hardware, and the server can run air-gapped.

points.title: Discounts for students and retirees
points.text: Pro licenses are 80% off for students aged 27 or under and retirees, for non-commercial use, and 50% off for teaching staff. Cloud plans have no discounts.

points.title: Windows: per-user installer or zip
points.text: The Windows build installs for the current user in 64-bit and 32-bit versions, and a zip is also offered. The Windows listing keeps 50 versions; macOS, which needs version 14 or later, lists only the current release.
